items.title: Pay import charges for held parcel (likely scam – do not pay before verifying)
items.computation: Calendar date printed in the letter: 09.11.2026. It is a Monday, not a holiday in NRW, so no adjustment. Note: the letter is dated 05.11.2026 (Thursday), leaving very little time.

warnings: Likely scam: real customs charges are demanded by German customs (Zoll) or the postal carrier, not by a private 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.' to a personal IBAN; verify with the carrier or the Zoll before paying anything.
Short deadline and threat of return or destruction of the parcel are typical pressure tactics.
Queries are allowed only via WhatsApp, and the email domain is a generic 'clearance-mail.example' address, both common signs of fraud.
The letter names no sender, no customs reference (such as a MRN or customs notice) and gives no legal remedy instructions.
The letter does not say what the parcel contains or who sent it, and the amounts (21.40 + 17.50 = 38.90) include a vague 'processing fee'.
The recipient's postcode 37073 belongs to Göttingen (Lower Saxony), not NRW, although the address city is given as 'Neu-Beispielstadt'. Double-check the address details.

The system prompt context gives two different 'today' dates (2026-11-07 and 2026-09-30); I used 2026-11-07 from the user's message, so the payment deadline may be in two days or may still be weeks away.
